2: A young woman who has reached maturity (meaning she has developed two pubic hairs) is not permitted to let herself become disheveled during mourning. Rather, she should adorn herself so that potential suitors will be attracted to her. However, a girl who is not yet of marriageable age—until she matures—is allowed to let herself go unkempt, because she is obligated in the laws of mourning. As for a minor (a girl who has not reached maturity), she has no obligation in mourning practices at all.

During the days of mourning for her father – even if she is in mourning because her brother died, or even if it was her own father who passed away, although she is of an age where she is obligated to observe the laws of mourning, she is not permitted to let herself become disheveled or unattractive.
